t:
Section 2 (b) of title III of article I of said Act is amended by adding thereto the following new paragraph:


“(14) 
Dues and initiation fees in the case of any club organized and operated exclusively for pleasure and recreation, no part of the net earnings of which inures to the benefit of any private individual or shareholder. As used in this subsection, the word ‘dues’ means only sums paid or incurred by members on a monthly, quarterly, annual, or other periodic basis for the privilege of being members of such club and any pro rata assessment made against the members as such; the word ‘dues’ does not include any sums paid or incurred by members or their guests for food, beverages, or other tangible personal property purchased or for the use of the club’s social, athletic, sporting, and other facilities; and the term ‘initiation fees’ includes any payment, contribution, or loan, required as a condition precedent to membership, whether or not any such payment, contribution, or loan is evidenced by a certificate of interest or indebtedness.”

fable.w: This section amends a tax provision to add and define an item covering club dues and initiation fees. The tempting reading is that words like 'members' and 'club' suggest membership or participation, but they refer to members of private recreational clubs, not to outside parties taking part in a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, rulemaking authority, or right to sue.
fable.s: Dues and initiation fees in the case of any club organized and operated exclusively for pleasure and recreation

qwen_block.w: This section defines terms related to tax deductions for dues and initiation fees for recreational clubs. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in a federal decision-making process. The text is purely definitional and regulatory regarding tax code provisions.
qwen_block.s: Dues and initiation fees in the case of any club organized and operated exclusively for pleasure and recreation, no part of the net earnings of which inures to the benefit of any private individual or shareholder.

opus.w: This amendment only adds club dues and initiation fees to a tax provision and defines those terms. No federal decision involves consultation, a hearing, comment, rulemaking or a right to sue. Club members paying dues are not taking part in any government decision, so words like "members" and "assessment" do not make this participation.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is to treat club "members" paying "dues" and "assessments" as people taking part in something. That doesn't fit the DEFINITION. The provision only defines which club dues and initiation fees fall under a tax provision. No federal decision involves any outside party: there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking authority, advisory body or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section provides a definition for tax purposes regarding dues and initiation fees for recreational clubs. It does not require the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or receive input from outside parties (such as club members or the general public) before making a decision. It is a substantive rule defining terms, not a procedural requirement for public participation.
qwen_chat.s: Dues and initiation fees in the case of any club organized and operated exclusively for pleasure and recreation, no part of the net earnings of which inures to the benefit of any private individual or shareholder.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that defining "dues" and "initiation fees" involves the public (club members) in some way, or that the mention of "members" implies participation. However, this is merely a definitional clause for tax purposes. It does not require the government to consult with club members, hold hearings, or coordinate with outside entities before making a decision. It simply clarifies what constitutes taxable or non-taxable income for specific types of organizations. There is no procedural requirement for outside involvement in a federal decision-making process.
